away.headline: Iowa State women's coach Bill Fennelly suspended for a game for `inappropriate contact' with player
away.source: The Associated Press- Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Fennelly will sit out at Northern Iowa on Wednesday night. Associate head coach Caroline McCombs will direct the team that night. AMES, Iowa (AP) — Iowa State suspended women’s basketball coach Bill Fennelly one game Sunday night for “inappropriate contact” with a Cyclones player. Fennelly nudged the player’s head with his hand earlier Sunday in a 69-64 home victory over Illinois Chicago. The 69-year-old Bill Fennelly said last month he plans to retire at the end of the season, his 32nd as head coach at the school. “We cannot tolerate inappropriate contact between a coach or staff member and a student-athlete in practice or in competition, whether intentional or not,” athletic director Jared Benko said in a statement. “We have high expectations of all of our coaches, staff and student-athletes and we will not shy away from holding accountable those who fail to meet those expectations. I have met with Coach Fennelly and he has apologized to the student-athlete involved and regrets his actions.” “I want to apologize to the student-athlete and her family, her teammates and all of Cyclone Nation for allowing my emotions to get the best of me during our game,” Fennelly said in a statement. “I fully recognize that there are no situations where it is appropriate to make contact with a student-athlete in that way. I accept responsibility and will serve the suspension and I will do better moving forward.” The Cyclones are 5-0 this season. Fennelly is 661-335 with 24 NCAA Tournament appearances and 26 postseason appearances at Iowa State. home.headline: RB Duke Watson Headlines UCF Injury Report Ahead of Arizona State Game
home.blurb: While UCF is without key players, the team could get linebacker Lewis Carter back, as he's listed as probable. Carter has missed every conference game starting from Week 4. The 6-foot senior is UCF's heart of the front seven. He leads as the captain, calling out offensive adjustments and communicating with his teammates. Carter's potential return bolsters a deep linebacker corps that's held the fort. He's joining Tackett Curtis, Jahleel Culbreath, Jayden Jennings and Cole Kozlowski in the front seven. Grinch said he feels better when Carter is out on the field quarterbacking the defense. RB Duke Watson Headlines UCF Injury Report Ahead of Arizona State Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF RB Duke Watson Headlines UCF Injury Report Ahead of Arizona State Game (Mike Watters/Imagn Images) Demetrius Montero · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:42 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Running back Duke Watson headlines a lengthy UCF Knights injury report ahead of their home game against the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday. Watson was carted off the field in last Saturday's thriller win over the Kansas Jayhawks . He wore street clothes and a boot on his right foot on the sidelines. Coach Scott Frost couldn't provide an update on the junior's status in his weekly press conference on Monday. Frost said he'd learn more Monday evening, and now the Knights will be without their speedster workhorse. The junior has 596 yards and three touchdowns on 94 carries this season. He's a big playmaker, bursting through open gaps with blazing speed for momentum-shifting runs. Watson has two longest rushes of 60-plus yards, both in non-conference play against the Bethune-Cookman Wildcats and Georgia State Panthers. UCF's No. 1 running back joins six other Knights who will miss Saturday's game: defensive backs Demari Henderson, DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson; offensive lineman Tyler Gibson and tight end Dylan Burk. Henderson is arguably UCF's most-valuable defensive player this season. He became the second Knight with two or more multi-interception games, recording two interceptions and adding seven tackles in Week 3's win over the Georgia State Panthers. The Big 12 awarded him the Defensive Player of the Week honors for his stellar performance. The redshirt senior is a Swiss Army knife for the Knights' defense, playing multiple assignments. UCF has missed his presence over the middle, especially in second-half collapses against ranked foes. The then-No. 20 Houston Cougars and then-No. 18 Oklahoma State Cowboys repeatedly completed passes over the linebackers' zones to walk down the Knights. The Knights are one win away from snapping a two-season bowl drought. Getting back a major defensive addition shores up the middle of the field and gives defensive coordinator Alex Grinch peace of mind.

home.headline: UCF Running Back Ruled Out For Arizona State Game: Injury Report Breakdown
home.blurb: UCF Running Back Ruled Out For Arizona State Game: Injury Report Breakdown Skip to main content SI.COM The highest-profile name officially out for Saturday's game against the Sun Devils is running back Duke Watson , UCF's primary rusher so far this season. He had just two carries last Saturday in Lawrence before an injury took him out of the game. He was shown on ESPN2's broadcast later in the game in street clothes and wearing a walking boot. Watson's injury comes fresh off the return of fellow running back Taevion Swint , who was out for two games with an injury of his own. He now stands to gain some more touches due to Watson's absence alongside Landen Chambers , who had his own injury during the Kansas game, but his absence from the Knights' Wednesday report indicates he is a go for Saturday. While the Knights are going to be without one rusher against Arizona State, there is a chance they may also be without two pass catchers as well, as wide receiver Waden Charles has been designated doubtful and tight end Caden Piening has been designated questionable . FRIDAY UPDATE: Charles was offically ruled out for Saturday's game in the Knights' Friday report. Quarterback Keyone Jenkins was designated questionable on Wednesday, though with Alonza Barnett III back and healthy, his status is more of a question about who the Knights' backup quarterback is going to be. Should Jenkins need to sit another game, freshman Rocco Marriott , who saw the field briefly in Kansas, would likely take up the role. All three of the Knights' defensive backs that were sidelined last weekend against Kansas: Demari Henderson , DJ Bell and Kahmel Johnson are once again ruled out for Saturday's game against Arizona State. This is going to mark Henderson's third missed game of the season, the third for Bell and the second for Johnson. The sidelined trio were not the only defensive backs featured in UCF's report, as Antione Jackso n and Ty Bartrum were both designated probable on Wednesday. Bartrum was labeled probable last weekend as well and went on to play. So, barring any setbacks, both should see the field on Saturday. After missing the first six games of conference play, linebacker Lewis Carter is on the verge of returning to the field after receiving a probable designation. Coach Scott Frost said he had his fingers crossed for him during his Monday press conference. Carter's return would actually make UCF's linebacker room deeper. In the time he's been injured, Cole Kozlowski was given a temporary injunction that allowed him to play for the Knights this season. So, accounting for Carter's return, UCF could now feature a five-man rotation at linebacker with Carter, Kozlowski, Tackett Curtis , Jahleel Culbreath and Jayden Jennings , the latter of which was also designated probable for Saturday's game. UCF is going to be without offensive lineman Tyler Gibson , listed as the backup right tackle behind Preston Cushman on the Knights' depth chart, for a fifth straight game

home.headline: UCF football linebacker Lewis Carter reflects on return from injury
UCF RB Duke Watson Status for Arizona State, Scott Frost Comments
home.blurb: The UCF Knights got some bad news ahead of their home game against the Arizona State Sun Devils on Saturday. Wednesday availability reports shared that running back Duke Watson is going to be out. After that game, UCF head coach Scott Frost confirmed it was a foot injury. The exact severity wasn't clear at the time. The team hasn't clarified the exact nature of his injury since then, but it's clearly bad enough to keep him out for some time. With Watson out, UCF is likely going to turn to a mixture of Landen Chambers and Taevion Swint against Arizona State. However, Frost also did bring up Agyeman Addae, who has been coming on strong lately in that running back room. UCF RB Duke Watson Status for Arizona State, Scott Frost Comments Watson was injured early in last week's win against Kansas. He would be tackled awkwardly, and despite making it off the field under his own power would be carted to the locker room. Watson later returned to the UCF sidelines in street clothes and a walking boot. Unfortunately, for UCF, Watson wasn't the only running back to get injured against Kansas. Landen Chambers also left later in the game. He did not appear on the Wednesday availability report, a good sign. Duke Watson Has Been Vital to the UCF Knights A transfer into UCF, Duke Watson has been the team's best running back all season long. That's helped the Knights to lean on the running game and overcome some injuries at quarterback. In nine games, Watson has 596 yards on 94 carries to go along with 3 touchdowns. That's 6.34 yards per carry. He also has 8 receptions for 15 yards. That has made Watson by far the most productive running back for UCF this season. Landen Chambers is second on UCF in rushing, but he only has 225 yards on 4.1 yards per carry. Then, Taevion Swint is third with 181 yards on 4.5 yards per carry. They've combined for 7 rushing touchdowns. With quarterback Alonza Barnett healthy, they'll have his dimension in the running game. Defenses will also have to respect him as a passer, opening up running lanes. Still, it's clear that UCF is going to need their depth at running back to step up in a major way during the home stretch of the season. After all, they're now just one win shy of bowl eligibility for the first time since 2023. UCF HC Scott Frost Addressed the Running Back Room On Wednesday night, Scott Frost had his weekly coach's show. There, he would address the running back situation. "Swint's back," Frost said . "And I feel good about him, and I think Landen's going to be good. But AG's ready to go, too, if we need him." Addae is a sophomore who came to UCF as a walk-on a season ago. This season, he has six carries for 74 yards, or 12.3 yards per carry, and a touchdown. He also flashed some nice play late against Kansas. "AG's practiced a lot, and he's made some plays for us," Frost said. Certainly, it seems like UCF has the depth at running back to overcome the Watson injury, at least for the time being. home.headline: UCF Q&A: How does Lewis Carter’s return help the Knights?
home.blurb: “Lewis, like a lot of our guys, he's been out a long time,” said coach Scott Frost . “He’s going to continue to get better as he gets closer to 100% and shakes the rust off a little bit. He’s a great person and a great player. He’s one of our leaders and we’ve missed him.” Florida & Caribbean Experiences Branded Content Paid Partner Content Services About the Orlando Sentinel 🎁 Gift idea: Sentinel's 150th book This was supposed to be Lewis Carter ‘s breakout season. Instead, the UCF linebacker and team captain found himself on the sideline with an injury that cost him half the season. Carter, 22, returned against Arizona State on Saturday, playing for the first time since Sept. 19 against Georgia State. “I was flying around and had a lot of energy. It felt good,” said Carter, who finished with three tackles on 25 snaps. In Carter’s absence, transfer Tackett Curtis has emerged as the team’s leading tackler (67), along with Jahleel Culbreath (44), Jaden Jennings (23), and Cole Kozlowski (19), who returned after a court order in fall camp. Carter spent much of his time off the field mentoring his teammates. “I was being hands-on as much as I could within the meeting rooms and on the sidelines,” said Carter. “I was trying to be a voice for the guys throughout.” How important are turnovers against Iowa State? Iowa State has turned the ball over just nine times — tied for the second-fewest turnovers given up in the Big 12 this season. Meanwhile, UCF has struggled to create takeaways lately, failing to force a turnover for the second time in its last three games. The Knights are 1-9 under Frost when they don’t force a miscue, including an 0-3 mark this season. “At times, we’ve been really good and the games where we’ve gotten turnovers, we’ve won those games,” said Frost. “That’s no secret. That’s the biggest stat in football.” Frost credits the takeaways with not only giving the team much-needed momentum, but also shortening the field and giving the offense more chances to score. Something the Knights could use more of over the remaining two games. How can the Knights get more pressure on the quarterback? UCF has gone back-to-back games without sacking a quarterback for the first time since 2021. The Knights have 16 sacks heading into this week’s showdown, tied for the second-fewest in the Big 12 with Iowa State. “We’ve actually gotten a lot of pressure, but we haven’t gotten the sacks,” said Frost. “As far as affecting throws, our guys have been pretty good. We’ve just got to finish those plays. There were at least three the other night when he had free shots and didn’t get the quarterback down.” While UCF hopes to finish strong, the Knights' focus is on Iowa State UCF needs quicker start, O-line struggles | Five takeaways from Arizona State loss Pictures: UCF vs Arizona State Football Lackluster performance sends UCF to a frustrating loss to Arizona State UCF-Arizona State kickoff pushed back to 5:30 p.m. due to travel issues The defense press

As interim offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas previewed Nebraska's Senior Day matchup with the Buckeyes, freshman running back Jamal Rule was among the players who earned his praise. Here's what Thomas had to say Tuesday about the Huskers' offensive approach heading into their final home game of 2026. The freshman bounced back in a big way against Rutgers , carrying the ball 22 times for 103 yards. When Thomas was asked about Rule's performance and recovery from the injury, he was was quick to praise his progress. “He’s been great,” Thomas said. “He’s really turned the corner and is running hard. What excites you as much as anything is his physicality, but also his ability to make some yards after contact. First play of the game, safety comes up and, you know, makes some contact, and he was able to get six or eight yards after that.” “Those are the things that we continue to try and promote and be aware of,” Thomas continued. “Cause, you know, if you block a four-yard run, you want to get six or eight; you don’t want to get a four-yard run. He’s really taken the next step since the injury. He’s playing fast; he’s playing confident; he’s physical. “He’s still a work in progress as far as having, you know, all the offseason, lack of reps. picks.blurb: Nebraska vs. Ohio State Odds: Can the Huskers Overcome the Buckeyes in Final Home Game of 2026? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day PISCATAWAY, NJ - NOVEMBER 14: Luke Lindenmeyer #8 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the game against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights at SHI Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:22 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Well, would you look at that? Nebraska just shut out a Big Ten opponent on the road. The Huskers dispatched Rutgers 31–0 on Saturday, and while the Scarlet Knights aren't exactly setting the college football world on fire, shutting out a conference opponent is no small accomplishment. Now comes Ohio State. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Ohio State mascot Brutus joins the Ohio State Buckeyes in the singing of "Carmen Ohio" following a 28-19 victory over the Northwestern Wildcats at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Normally, that name alone would be enough to make Nebraska fans start calculating how much bourbon they'll need by halftime. But these aren't the same Buckeyes we've grown accustomed to seeing. Ohio State has three losses. Three! In Columbus, that's practically grounds for declaring a state of emergency. And according to Ramsey from Eleven Warriors, who joined Monday Night Therapy this week, the problems aren't imaginary. The offensive line has struggled. The tight ends apparently believe blocking is an optional extracurricular activity. Special teams have been an adventure, and not the enjoyable kind. The Buckeyes are also starting true freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, who's talented but still learning on the job. Those are a lot of vulnerabilities for a program accustomed to simply reloading every season. Of course, Ohio State still has Jeremiah Smith. COLUMBUS, OHIO - NOVEMBER 14: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes runs with the ball as Damon Walters #21 of the Northwestern Wildcats defends during the fourth quarter of a game at Ohio Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Columbus, Ohio. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images And therein lies the problem. Smith might be the best receiver in college football. Nebraska can scheme, disguise coverages, and pressure the quarterback all afternoon, but Smith is capable of making one play that changes everything. So how does Nebraska keep him from doing that? Run. The. Damn. Ball. Control possession. Move the chains. Keep the clock running. Make Ohio State's offense spend as much time watching from the sideline as possible. And when it's third-and-two, perhaps we could actually gain two yards instead of getting unnecessarily creative. Just a thought. Nebraska's defense has momentum after its performance against Rutgers, and a home crowd in Lincoln should make life uncomfortable for a freshman quarterback. The opportunity is there. But opportunity and execution haven't always been particularly close friends in Lincoln. Nebraska vs. Ohio State Betting Odds The betting discussion has centered on Ohio State as a narrow favorite. The FanDuel Sportsbook currently has the visitors as a 3.5-point favorite. The over/under is currently 41.5 points. Personally, I think Ohio State would deserve to be favored by six or seven points on a neutral field. But Memorial Stadium isn't neutral, and this isn't an Ohio State team without weaknesses. The Buckeyes have the talent to win this game. Nebraska has the opportunity to make that talent irrelevant for long stretches. Whether the Huskers can actually pull that off is another question entirely. Choose wisely. Play responsibly. And Go Big Red. Always.

By Juan Pablo Aravena in College Football Published: November 17, 2026 at 12:05 pm EST My early Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction looks at whether the Huskers can carry their momentum into a home date with the Buckeyes The early Ohio State vs Nebraska spread leaves little room between the Buckeyes and the home underdog See my Ohio State vs Nebraska spread analysis and Big Ten picks below Ohio State visits Nebraska on Saturday, Nov. 21, with a noon ET kickoff at Memorial Stadium. The Buckeyes are 7-3 overall and 5-2 in Big Ten play after a 28-19 win over Northwestern, which followed a 41-28 loss to Oregon. Nebraska is 6-4 and 3-4 in conference play. The Huskers bounced back from a 24-13 loss to Illinois by blanking Rutgers 31-0. Three points is the key number in Lincoln. Here's my Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction and the price that makes the total my first bet. Ohio State vs Nebraska Prediction Prediction: Ohio State wins a close game; I like the Over more than laying points with the Buckeyes My Ohio State vs Nebraska prediction is that this stays close. The Buckeyes are the likelier winner, but Nebraska has the recent form and the home crowd to keep it within a field goal. Ohio State's offense still runs through Jeremiah Smith. He has 80 catches for 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns. The Buckeyes have been forced to rely on Luke Fahey under center due to the absence of Julian Sayin due to injury. Fahey completed 21 of 32 passes for 201 yards, three touchdowns and one interception during Saturday's 28-19 win over Northwestern in Week 11. Bo Jackson gives the Buckeyes balance with 799 rushing yards and seven scores on 159 carries. The question is the defense. Ohio State gave up 41 points to Oregon and 19 to Northwestern in its last two games. Nebraska, meanwhile, just pitched a shutout. Jahsear Whittington leads the Huskers with 5.5 sacks, and pressure on Fahey is Nebraska's best path to keeping this tight. The risk to a close-game prediction is Smith winning outside early. Two chunk completions can put Nebraska two scores behind before its run game gets established. I'd consider the Huskers at more than a field goal; at exactly three, a field-goal loss gets my stake back but doesn't win the bet. Ohio State vs Nebraska Spread Over 41.5 (-108) Under 41.5 (-111) Ohio State vs Nebraska odds via BetMGM as of Tuesday, November 17. Lines can move before Saturday. The Ohio State vs Nebraska spread makes the Buckeyes a field-goal favorite, but the prices aren't symmetrical. Laying three costs -118; taking the three costs -102. If both sides finish the day three points apart in Ohio State's favor, either spread bet pushes. Nebraska's +130 moneyline needs an outright win. That is a different call from my expectation that the Huskers stay in it. I'd rather see whether a +3.5 appears than turn a close-game forecast into an upset bet. The total sits at 41.5. A 24-18 game gets there; 23-17 does not. Shop the number as well as the price across College Football betting apps before Saturday. Ohio State vs Nebraska Big Ten Picks Big Ten pick: Over 41.5 points (-108 at BetMGM ) My second Big Ten pick is the Over. The market expects a low-scoring game, but both offenses have legitimate playmakers. Anthony Colandrea has thrown for 2,297 yards and 18 touchdowns for Nebraska. Kwazi Gilmer has turned 46 catches into 603 yards and seven scores, and Jamal Rule adds 635 rushing yards. Ohio State's last two games produced 47 and 69 total points. Nebraska doesn't have to match the Buckeyes touchdown for touchdown to clear 41.5: two touchdowns and a field goal for the Huskers would leave Ohio State needing 25 points. That fits a competitive game in the fourth quarter. A 24-21 Ohio State win would cash the Over while pushing both sides of the current spread. Chasing a first-half winner would require another forecast entirely; I'm sticking to the full game. The Under wins if Nebraska's defense plays like it did against Rutgers. Colandrea's seven interceptions are the other risk, since empty possessions keep the scoreboard quiet. away.headline: What happened to quarterback Julian Sayin? Will he return to Ohio State?
away.blurb: “What we're trying to do is give Julian and his family the space and privacy to go through this process,” Day said Oct. 20. “But based on the nature of the injury, we are putting together a plan for him not being available for the regular season and then also him not being available for the postseason. “If he's not able to return this fall, then we're putting a plan together for that as well. That's the update I have right now." When asked about the possibility of Sayin returning before the end of the regular season, Day said, “I try not to get in any kind of timeline on that. To think that that's going to happen is doubtful.” Sayin has been behind center for the Buckeyes for more than a year, having made 21 consecutive starts since he beat out Lincoln Kienholz in a preseason competition in 2025. Will Julian Sayin return to Ohio State? "When you stack him against the other top draft-eligible arms, he lands toward the back of the pack," Baumgardner wrote on Oct. 4. "He’s not real big, and his arm strength is pretty limited. He’s very smart, though. He knows where to go with the ball, doesn’t get stuck too much and can be really accurate." If Sayin does return to Ohio State, it also seems likely that he would regain his starting role. His backup, Fahey, has struggled to throw passes downfield in his first two starts. Before camp, it was presumed that quarterback Tavien St. Clair would move up after spending last year as the third-stringer. St. Clair stood out during the spring game in April. The native of Bellefontaine, who was the first Ohio high school quarterback since Joe Burrow to sign a scholarship agreement with Ohio State, was a highly touted five-star prospect. A five-star recruit out of Bellefontaine High School, St. Clair was the second-ranked quarterback from the Class of 2024, according to 247Sports, slotting behind Michigan's Bryce Underwood. St. Clair ended as the runner-up for the Mr. Football title, as junior quarterback Matt Ponatoski out of Cincinnati Moeller beat him out by 10 points (70-60). In the fourth quarter of a a 19-15 win at Indiana on Oct. 17, Sayin was hurt when he was sacked early in the fourth quarter. Defensive lineman Mario Landino collided with Sayin as he began to attempt a pass, causing his arm to bend awkwardly. Sayin had to exit the game early. After leaving for the locker room, he returned with his right throwing arm in a sling. Quarterback Luke Fahey finished the fourth quarter for OSU and started in losses to USC and Oregon. Ohio State coach Ryan Day said the Buckeyes are taking account the possibility Sayin will miss the rest of 2026. What has Julian Sayin done at Ohio State? Sayin finished fourth in the voting for the Heisman Trophy last year with one of the most accurate single seasons for a passer in the Football Bowl Subdivision. home.headline: Andrew Marshall injury could keep Nebraska from taking the next step in evolution
home.blurb: Marshall missed the Huskers’ game against Rutgers this past weekend, and on Monday, head coach Matt Rhule confirmed that the star defensive back is out for the rest of the season. When Nebraska faces off against Ohio State on Saturday, the Huskers know they won’t have to face quarterback Julian Sayin . However, they’ll still have to face all-time great wide receiver Jeremiah Smith, which is why losing Andrew Marshall is a big blow. Rhule said that Marshall suffered a stress fracture in his leg against Illinois but continued to play after suffering the injury. Since that game, Marshall has undergone surgery to repair the fracture and has played his last down for Nebraska in his college football career. Marshall finished the 2026 season with 28 tackles, an interception, and a team-high six pass breakups. He’s long been considered one of the best defensive backs in the country, and Rhule made that point when addressing the injury. Andrew Marshall season-ending injury leaves Nebraska football without shutdown corner vs. Ohio State “I think he’s as good as there is in the country and I think everyone knows it,” Rhule said during his Monday press conference. “I think everyone’s seen it.” The California native is one of NU’s best transfer-portal stories after arriving from Idaho before the 2025 campaign. Nebraska routinely lined him up opposite an opponent’s best receiver and often left him in one-on-one coverage while devoting defensive help elsewhere. Marshall was targeted just 44 times this season and allowed just 15 receptions for 237 yards. 93 of those yards came against Illinois, as it was easily his worst game of the season. Playing on a bum leg certainly explains why he struggled against Illinois’ Colin Dixon, who was recently named to the latest Fred Biletnikoff Award watch list. Nebraska started Victor Evans and freshman Danny Odem at cornerback against Rutgers and will move forward with the same duo along with Jeremiah Charles. Junior Larry Tarver is also set to see more rotational action. Without Nebraska’s shutdown corner, beating Ohio State became even tougher on Monday. It’s unlikely that one corner will be assigned to Smith the way defensive coordinator Rob Aurich might have assigned Marshall if he were healthy. Nebraska is obviously hoping that a change in offensive coordinator and the end of the four-game losing streak will allow the Huskers to finish the season strong. Beating Ohio State in Lincoln is never easy, but this version of the Buckeyes has shown they are flawed. There's no other way to slice it or dice it, it was disgraceful at best and a 'fire everybody in the whole football department' at worst. Which is what many of the Wisconsin fans are calling for. Maryland had only one Big Ten game all season and had fired their head coach. The Terrapins are a basement-dwelling Big Ten team. So, what does Vegas do for Wisconsin when the Badgers take on another basement-dwelling team, Purdue? Well, they give them barely favorable odds. Can't trust them. The best thing Wisconsin has going for itself in this Purdue game is that it's the Boilermakers that the Terrapins beat a couple of games ago. The Badgers enter their final road game of the season against a *checks notes* 3-7 Purdue team as barely a favorite. At 5.5 points, Vegas assumes that Wisconsin can only beat the Boilermakers with two field goals... or worse. That's alarming and paints a bleak reality for Luke Fickell. In his banner year, the "prove-it" year, the one when everything lined up perfectly. He had the bigger budget, the supposedly better coaching staff, a deeper quarterback room, a way more favorable schedule, and yet, with only two games to go, Wisconsin is barely considered a favorite over Purdue. It's hard to express how disappointing that is, when Wisconsin should be looking at this game as a "rest the starters" in the 4th-quarter situation; they are staring down the barrel of another potential upset. If there's anything that shows Wisconsin should move on from Luke Fickell and/or some of his staff, it's this bleak reminder that the program is actually in the same place as last year, but with an easier schedule. ESPN has the probabilities a bit higher than Vegas at 65% according to their analytics, but still, that's not great. And if Wisconsin can't find a way to beat Purdue, and beat them without any drama, there's no reason Luke Fickell needs to get on the flight back to Madison. And yet the big fear is that this 6-win season will be sold to Wisconsin fans as a step forward and that the Badgers should continue to let him run it back. The $21 million buy-out may force Shawn Eichorst to gaslight the fanbase, as Chris McIntosh did. Hopefully, I'm wrong, but it feels like we are headed that direction. This Purdue game needs to be a blowout; winning by 5 or 6 points won't be good enough. Fans should be embarrassed that Vegas even suggests so. away.blurb: Wisconsin (6-4, 4-3) suffered a frustrating 24-21 loss Saturday at Maryland (4-6, 2-5), a result that only intensified questions surrounding the program's direction . Having already handed out grades for the offense , Badgers On SI now breaks down the defense and special teams. Donovan Dunmore was thrust into an expanded role at cornerback despite limited previous experience and showed promise as a tackler, finishing with seven tackles (four solo) and a tackle for loss. His coverage was less encouraging, as the freshman allowed receptions on all three targets for 36 yards and earned a 49.8 PFF coverage grade. The safety rotation was also disrupted when Matt Jung suffered an apparent leg injury while recovering a fumble near Wisconsin's goal line late in the second quarter. Matthew Traynor subsequently saw his first meaningful action, logging 30 snaps and finishing with six tackles (four solo) and a respectable 66.3 PFF overall grade. However, his fourth-quarter personal foul for a late hit out of bounds was a moment to forget. Darrion Dupree provided respectable production in the return game, totaling 56 yards on two kickoff returns, though neither produced a game-changing play. Overall, it was a fairly steady showing from Wisconsin's special teams outside of West's second-quarter miscue. Wisconsin Football Report Card: Injuries Take Their Toll on Badgers Defense Skip to main content SI.COM The absence of star edge rusher Sebastian Cheeks presented a challenge for Wisconsin's defensive front, and his presence was sorely missed. Tyreese Fearbry generated two pressures but failed to provide the necessary spark, earning a dismal 18.4 PFF tackling grade. Nick Clayton saw his workload increase to a career-high 45 snaps and made little impact as a pass rusher, though he fared well against the run and finished with five tackles (four solo). Nolan Vils was a bright spot along the interior, recording four tackles (two solo) and half a tackle for loss while earning a team-best 80.7 PFF overall grade. Defensive tackles Charles Perkins and Hammond Russell IV each generated a pressure, but Perkins struggled as a tackler, missing two tackles and receiving a 25.5 grade in that department. Collectively, Wisconsin held Maryland to 107 rushing yards on 39 attempts (2.7 YPC), another strong showing from a run defense that has been a consistent strength. However, the inability to generate meaningful pressure proved costly as backup quarterback Cardell Williams settled into a rhythm, completing 21-of-23 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown. The Badgers desperately need Cheeks back to bolster a pass rush that struggled to disrupt the Terrapins’ aerial attack. Avdalas is expected to miss a significant portion of North Carolina’s nonconference schedule, along with the beginning of ACC play, as he begins his recovery. During his freshman season with the Hokies, the 6-foot-9 guard averaged 12.1 points and 4.6 assists per game. He started all 31 games and earned ACC Rookie of the Week honors twice. (Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Trevor Woods · SB Nation Tue, November 17, 2026 at 12:44 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines are 5-5 and have a really tall task on Saturday at Michigan Stadium when they take on the No. 4 UCLA Bruins. The Bruins are 10-0 for the first time since 1998 and have had a remarkable season to this point under head coach Bob Chesney, who is in his first season with the program. While Michigan and UCLA have had seasons that are vastly different, betting odds seem to feel that this game could be closer than perceived. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Michigan is a 3.5-point underdog against UCLA, with the over/under set at 38.5 points. This is a dangerous spread for anyone betting on Michigan — the Wolverines are just 3-7 against the spread this season. Michigan was a 9.5-point underdog against Oregon last week and went on to lose 31-7. UCLA hasn't had the toughest schedule, but Michigan's offense is one of the worst in the nation, and it's yet another week of head coach Kyle Whittingham saying that it will be an open quarterback competition ahead of the game between Tommy Carr and Bryce Underwood. The betting odds must feel a West Coast team traveling to Ann Arbor in November could prove to be difficult, but the forecast on game day is currently showing it's going to be 63 degrees out — which is abnormally warm for Michigan this time of year. Then there's the tale of two coaches. UCLA head coach Bob Chesney could win coach of the year, while Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham could be one-and-done. There's every reason to believe UCLA will cover in this one.

The Bruins are rolling under first-year head coach Bob Chesney, and with two more regular-season games remaining, they have a chance to finish undefeated for the first time since 1954! Playing the role of spoiler this week are the Michigan Wolverines (5-5). Michigan has not lived up to expectations in their first year under Kyle Whittingham, as they’re currently scraping by to make a bowl game. With UCLA and Ohio State on the schedule, Michigan needs a massive upset win to reach bowl eligibility. Could it happen here? Not many people believe so, and the market pegs UCLA as a- 3.5-point road favorite with a game total of 37.5 points. In other words, don’t expect many points from either team. Will Michigan start Tommy Carr or Bryce Underwood this week? Whittingham said the two will battle it out after Carr replaced Underwood in the 31-7 loss to Oregon. UCLA outlasted Illinois, 22-14, on Friday night, but not without drama. The Bruins Ty Dieffenbach went down with an injury in the second quarter, then returned on the first drive of the fourth quarter following the Illini’s first score of the game (12-7). Like UCLA has done all season, they scored 10 points in the fourth quarter and had explosive plays left and right. UCLA built on their nation-leading 30 takeaways with three interceptions off Illinois and held the Illini to 240 total yards of offense. Let’s dive into the schools on both sides of the ball, look at a few key players, and see where the numbers take us. Game Details and How to Watch UCLA vs Michigan Date: Saturday, November 21, 2026 Time: 3:30 PM Eastern Site: Michigan Stadium City: Ann Arbor, MI TV/Streaming: CBS Game Odds for UCLA vs Michigan The latest odds as of Tuesday courtesy of DraftKings : Moneyline: UCLA Bruins (-185), Michigan Wolverines (+154) Spread: UCLA -3.5 (-112) Total: 37.5 points Head Coach: Bob Chesney 2026 Record: 10-0 (7-0) Offensive Points Per Game: 32.4 (34th) Defensive Points Per Game: 14.1 (6th) 2026 Strength of Schedule: 69th The UCLA Bruins Offense: UCLA outgained Illinois 361-240 in total yards and averaged 9.4 yards per pass and 3.2 yards per rush. Illinois managed six TFL, but only one sack on the Bruins. UCLA has outscored its opponents 112-34 in the fourth quarter this season and outscored Illinois 10-7 last Friday to outlast the Illini. In UCLA’s road games, the Bruins outscored Cal 21-0, Maryland 20-0, Minnesota 17-10, and were outscored by Oregon 9-7 in the fourth quarter. Michigan’s defense allows 7.4 points per game in the fourth quarter (83rd) and 6.6 at home. UCLA Player to Watch on Offense: QB Ty Dieffenbach Ty Dieffenbach is a tough guy. After exiting with an injury, he came back in to lead UCLA to another win. If he isn’t 100 percent, that could be an issue. Madden Iamaleava was unable to do much of anything in the second and third quarters (3/7 for 21 yards, one sack). The Michigan defense is brutal, and John Henry Daley leads a ferocious front seven that wants to get pressure and play man coverage with their elite corners. Teams have blundered under zone against UCLA recently, so I’ll be interested to see the coverages Michigan throws Dieffenbach’s way. The UCLA Bruins Defense: UCLA’s defense has been incredible this season and has been half the reason why the Bruins have been able to overcome Nico Iamaleava’s season-ending injury. UCLA has 30 takeaways this season (20 INTs, 10 FR) and grabbed three more last week. The Bruins held the Illini to 4.8 yards per pass and 2.1 yards per rush, plus grabbed two sacks, five TFL, and five pass deflections. UCLA has a positive matchup against a struggling Michigan offense, but the Bruins should expect to see some trickery and shots to try to loosen up Carr or Underwood against the daunting UCLA defense. UCLA Player to Watch on Defense: DB Scooter Jackson Scooter Jackson is on a run right now. UCLA has an NCAA-leading 30 takeaways, and he has contributed to that with a team-leading five interceptions and one forced fumble. Jackson has an interception in three straight games, including two of the team’s three picks against Illinois. He has at least one pass deflection in four straight games and a team-high seven on the season. Whoever starts at quarterback will be more than aware of Jackson’s interception streak. Who will start at quarterback? Tommy Carr has started the last four games and Michigan has scored 6, 28, 6, and 7 points for 11.7 points per game. If you take out Michigan’s 52 points in the UTEP outing, Bryce Underwood averaged 15.7 points per game in his first four full starts. The argemeunt will be you’re paying Underwood a ton of money, so might as well play him, whereas the other half would be Carr could be your future, so play him and see what you have. Maybe Michigan has seen enough. We’ll find out this Saturday. Michigan Player to Watch on Offense: The QB battle Michigan’s offense ranks 131st in points per game (18.3), so no matter who’s at quarterback this season won’t change much for the Wolverines. Tommy Carr replaced Bryce Underwood against Penn State and led a second half comeback before making his first career start the following week in an OT loss to Indiana (13-6). Underwood has a chance to prove his doubters wrong with an upset over UCLA or Ohio State if his name is called. The Michigan Wolverines Defense: The Michigan defense has been the bread and butter to their success this season. In wins, Michigan has held their opponents to 12, 10, 17, 18, and 21 points for 15.6 points per game. In losses, that number balloons to 19.9 points per game, but take away the Oregon outing last week and that number is 17.0 ppg. The Wolverines are coming off their worst outing of the season giving up a season-high in points (31), yards (467), and passing yards (341). Michigan Player to Watch on Defense: DL John Henry Daley John Henry Daley recorded his third-highest tackle total of the season with five, and didn’t record a sack against Oregon. Daley has 6.0 sacks on the season and two against Michigan, but the Ducks’ offensive line came up with plenty of schemes and double teams to slow him down. When he returned back to the sideline and re-entered the game in the second half, it gave the Bruins the surge they needed to keep their perfect season alive. Dieffenbach threw for 232 yards and two touchdowns while overcoming his injury, and No. 4 UCLA remained unbeaten with a rain-soaked, 22-14 victory over Illinois on Friday night. “The confidence I think that was gained from that, from him being back, and the confidence he was portraying and showing to them, exuding, that was certainly something that they all felt and understood,” UCLA coach Bob Chesney said. Dieffenbach left with 35 seconds to go in the first half after he fell hard on his left elbow and humerus following a hit by defensive lineman Carter Janki. Third-stringer Madden Iamaleava played the next three series for the Bruins as Dieffenbach remained in the locker room with his arm feeling “nervy”, according to Chesney. Dieffenbach returned with 55 seconds left in the third quarter to a loud ovation from the crowd. away.headline: UCLA's Semaj Morgan disses Michigan's Big House: 'Older fans, so it's not that loud'

He spent three seasons at Michigan, and played in every game of the national championship-winning campaign in 2023. In 37 games for the Wolverines , he had 69 catches for 566 yards with four touchdowns. He was also a two-time all-Big Ten honorable mention selection as a return specialist. UCLA leading receiver Semaj Morgan will have a homecoming in Week 12 of the college football season, returning to play at his old home in the Big House against Michigan. A Detroit native, the Bruins ' first road trip to Michigan since 1996 will also be the first time Morgan will play in the state after spending the previous three seasons in Ann Arbor. home.headline: Former Michigan WR Semaj Morgan takes shot at Big House crowd
home.blurb: In Ann Arbor, wide receiver Semaj Morgan had some highs and he had some lows. His punt return against Iowa in the 2023 Big Ten Championship Game and his touchdown against Texas in 2024 are among the highs. But numerous drops and struggles in the return game were among the lows. However, after a change of scenery to UCLA , Morgan is a man renewed, posting career highs with 41 catches for 525 yards and three touchdowns -- more than double any of his receiving yards any given season with Michigan football. His 525 yards would be second on this current Wolverines team, behind only JJ Buchanan, the star receiver who is out for the season now. Morgan is excited to return to The Big House with his undefeated Bruins , but he's also not trying to put too much on his return to the stadium he spent three years playing in. “Definitely, but the process is a process, and we got to keep going what we did to come this far,” Morgan said. “We don’t want to change the process based on our opponent. But it is kind of a special thing for me. I spent some time there, won a championship there, so it is going to be nice going back there. But I don’t want to overthink about it. I just want to keep the process.” Morgan has always been outspoken, if not blunt. When he shared his message to his UCLA teammates about what to expect about the environment at Michigan Stadium, he did not mince words. “Oh, yeah, I told them what it’s like,” Morgan said. “It’s a nice big stadium, older fans, so it’s not that loud, so we’re gonna have fun.” That might hold a kernel of truth, but given that UCLA struggles to even get the Rose Bowl to half full, it's not quite the dig that it could have otherwise been. Michigan and UCLA will kick off at 3:30 p.m. EST at The Big House, with the game set to be televised on CBS. home.blurb: While it sounds like a shot at his old school, Morgan did say the game will be a "special thing" for him. He spent three seasons at Michigan, and played in every game of the national championship-winning campaign in 2023. In 37 games for the Wolverines , he had 69 catches for 566 yards with four touchdowns. He was also a two-time all-Big Ten honorable mention selection as a return specialist. UCLA leading receiver Semaj Morgan will have a homecoming in Week 12 of the college football season, returning to play at his old home in the Big House against Michigan. A Detroit native, the Bruins ' first road trip to Michigan since 1996 will also be the first time Morgan will play in the state after spending the previous three seasons in Ann Arbor. REQUIRED READING: CFP rankings predictions: Texas has best résumé. How high will Longhorns climb now? From NFL plays to college sports scores, all the top sports news you need to know every day. But when it comes to playing at the biggest stadium in the United States as the road team, Morgan isn't concerned about the likely 110,000-plus fans in the stands, noting it isn't as loud as it may seem when he told his teammates about the conditions. "I told them what it's like. It's a nice, big stadium. Older fans, so it's not that loud," Morgan said. With UCLA, he has a team-high 41 catches for 525 yards for three touchdowns, a career year. "I spent some time there, won a championship there, so it is gonna be nice going back there. I don't wanna over think about it. I just want to keep the process, the process," he added. Morgan also said he's excited to see family again, and already let his mom know he's ready for a homecooked meal. "It'll be good to go back there and play a good game. I'm just really excited to go home, get to see my mom, my brothers, my niece," he said. At 10-0 with a 7-0 mark in the Big Ten, UCLA can clinch a spot in the Big Ten championship game with a win over the Wolverines. The Tigers have been at their worst against quality opponents, failing to cover in all four of their games against currently ranked teams. Lane Kiffin's offense has no-showed against top-tier defenses, averaging just 17 points and 2.5 turnovers per game against defenses ranked top 12 by SP+ . The Volunteers' defense is ranked No. 6 and is one of the most disruptive in the country. Jim Knowles' unit is No. 2 in sacks (39) and No. 3 in havoc rate (22.7%). That doesn't bode well for LSU QB Sam Leavitt , who's coming off the worst game of his career (five turnover-worthy plays) and has been a mess against the Tigers' best opponents. In four games against currently ranked teams, Leavitt has more interceptions (6) than TD passes (5) and has a 21.7% pressure-to-sack rate. And for as good as LSU's defense is, Tennessee's run game and offensive line are the best the Tigers have seen this season. DeSean Bishop has the Vols ranked No. 11 in EPA per rush and No. 17 in rush success rate (49.2%), and he should be able to wear LSU down enough to win a low-scoring game. By Juan Pablo Aravena in College Football Published: November 16, 2026 at 11:00 am EST Tennessee hosts a stumbling LSU team in a Week 12 SEC clash at Neyland Stadium. The LSU vs Tennessee betting line makes the Tigers a narrow road favorite in Knoxville. Read below for my early LSU vs Tennessee prediction and best bet for this SEC showdown The LSU Tigers travel to Knoxville to face the Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium on Saturday, November 21, 2026, with kickoff set for 3:30 p.m. ET. Tennessee enters on a two-game winning streak at 8-2 overall and 5-2 in SEC play. LSU arrives desperate to snap a two-game skid at 6-4 overall and 3-4 in the conference. The Tigers lost 31-13 to Alabama and then fell 22-21 to Texas last Saturday. My LSU vs Tennessee early prediction comes down to whether Tennessee can keep this game close enough for the point at home to matter. LSU vs Tennessee Early Prediction LSU vs Tennessee Betting Line LSU vs Tennessee SEC Picks Prediction: Tennessee covers as a short home underdog in a low-scoring game that stays Under the total My LSU vs Tennessee early prediction starts with the contrast in offensive identities. Tennessee runs through DeSean Bishop, who has 1,163 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns on 230 carries. That ground-and-pound approach bleeds the clock and shortens games. The Vols have not needed to lean on the pass. George MacIntyre leads the team with 962 passing yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions on 134 attempts, while Braylon Staley should be the No. 1 target in the passing game due to the fact that Mike Matthews is expected to miss the rest of the season with a knee injury. LSU is far more pass-heavy. Sam Leavitt has thrown for 2,797 yards with 19 touchdowns, but his 12 interceptions are a real concern on the road. Jackson Harris is his go-to receiver with 864 yards and nine touchdowns, and Dilin Jones adds 838 rushing yards and eight scores. Those interceptions matter against a Tennessee defense led by Tyree Weathersby (seven sacks) and Arion Carter (66 tackles). LSU has its own disruptors in Princewill Umanmielen (9.5 sacks) and TJ Dottery (73 tackles), so I expect both offenses to face steady pressure. Recent scoring backs a slower game. Four of Tennessee's last five games finished with 41 or fewer combined points, including a 22-7 win at Texas A&M. Three of LSU's last five also stayed at 44 or below. away.blurb: For No. 8 Texas (8-2, 5-2), the dreams of the playoffs continue while LSU will look to still get the taste of defeat out of its mouth as it hits the road next week to face No. 9 Tennessee at 2:30 p.m. CT on Saturday, Nov. 21 inside Neyland Stadium in Knoxville. Longhorns have the ball but if you're an LSU fan, your defense is the unit you want on the field to try and close this game out. Tigers have limited Texas to just 217 yards of offense and have forced three turnovers. Slowly but surely, Texas is getting back into this game as Gianni Spetic knocks in his third field goal of the game. He knocked this one in from 50 yards out to shrink LSU's lead to just five points. The Tigers have been living and dying in the air for the most part of this game until running back Dillin Jones found a lane. Jones broke out for a 44-yard rushing touchdown to extend LSU's lead. The run marks the longest rush of the night so far as both teams haven't run it a ton with success. That last possession of the half for LSU was a dud. Once the offense got close to the end zone, Texas' defense bowed up and LSU fizzled out. Leavitt just lobbed that ball up. I know the pressure is in his face but he's got to rifle that ball out of the back of the end zone. LSU OC Charlies Weis Jr. had Leavitt roll out plenty to avoid Texas' army of pass rushers. Get used to seeing that a lot tonight. After falling to Alabama last Saturday and suffering its third loss on the 2026 season, LSU couldn’t afford to lose against Texas inside Tiger Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 14. With their backs against the wall Lane Kiffin and his Tigers (6-4, 3-4 SEC) battled for every point while also trying to neutralize Texas’ star quarterback Arch Manning. In the end, Manning pulled off the second half heroics to help the Longhorns storm back and beat LSU 22-21. Thus ending the Tigers dream of making it to the College Football Playoff. It was far from pretty on offense for the Tigers. Quarterback Sam Leavitt matched his season-high in interceptions, throwing three. Interceptions were the theme of the night, with both Leavitt and Manning combining for six picks. Despite it, Manning and company only needed the final two minutes to go right as he finished the night throwing for 174 yards and a 4-yard game-winning touchdown. Defensively, LSU held the Longhorns to a season-low in points as they brought pressure almost every snap, making it hard for Manning to do what he does best; use he’s legs and pick defenses apart. picks.blurb: Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Week 11 Waiver Wire Spurs can't lose NFL Power Rankings Tiger return set Arch's senior day Story by Roundtable Sports Notre Dame Opponent Preview: SMU Mustangs (Jerome Miron, USA TODAY Sports) Trevor Trowbridge · Roundtable Sports Tue, November 17, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time since 1989, the Notre Dame Fighting Irish will host the SMU Mustangs inside of Notre Dame Stadium. Their last meeting didn't go too well for the visiting Mustangs as the Irish won 59-6 and took their foot off the gas relatively early in the second half. This year, however, it's a different looking SMU team that travels up north. This program is two years removed from playing for the ACC title and making the first ever 12-team College Football Playoffs. They have talent littered all over the field and will look to play spoiler to Notre Dame's Senior Day and their College Football Playoff hopes. Location : Notre Dame Stadium (Notre Dame, Ind.) Date : Saturday - November 21 Time : 7:30 PM ET TV : NBC/Peacock Line : Notre Dame -20.5; O/U 56.5 Let's kick off our preview of this matchup with an overview look at the SMU Mustangs Record at SMU : 45-19 (5th season) SMU head coach Rhett Lashlee is in the midst of his fifth season at the helm. Like the coach he's facing this Saturday, Marcus Freeman , he has had a winning record in every season he's been the head coach. In 2023 and 2024, the Mustangs posted back to back 11-3 seasons, playing for the ACC title in 2024 and making the College Football Playoffs. Unfortunately, they lost soundly on the road against Penn State but that didn't take away from the great season he had. Last year, expectations were at an all-time high for Lashlee and SMU and they entered as one of the favorites to win the league. Unfortunately, they ended their season at 9-4 and weren't able to handle business down the stretch to get back to the ACC title game. This year, SMU is looking similar to the 2025 version of themselves rather than the 2023 and 2024 versions, but a win over Notre Dame in South Bend could drastically change the outlook of their season. Lashlee has the talent to compete with some of the top teams in the country at certain spots, but he needs to put it all together to make it back to the CFP which likely won't happen this season. In some ways, he's having the season many thought he would, but his abilities as a runner have not been utilized by the offensive coaching staff. To a degree, it's understandable given the talent on the perimeter with players like Yamir Knight , Jalen Cooper , Yannick Smith , Jalen Hale , Theo Melin Ohrstrom and Randy Pittman Jr. requiring a lot of touches. Their defense has been the area of struggle this season, as it was last season. In many areas, Maurice Crum Jr ., a former Notre Dame captain at linebacker, has changed the outlook of the defense for the better. But they're a 'feast or famine' type of unit ranking 13th in the country in tackles for loss and 20th in the country in sacks but also ranking 110th in the country in passing touchdowns allowed and 128th in the country in red zone scoring allowed. This season, when they've faced offenses that can score, they've allowed 41 points to Louisville, 30 points to Syracuse and 49 points to Wake Forest. away.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
away.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. Full Notre Dame availability report Will Black, offensive lineman — concussion Francis Brewu, defensive lineman — left knee Brauntae Johnson, safety — left foot Jason Onye, defensive lineman — right knee Drayk Bowen, linebacker — right ankle Christopher Burgess Jr., defensive lineman — left tibia Tiki Hola, defensive lineman — right knee DJ McKinney, cornerback — right ankle Stay up to date on local news with WNDU on-air and online. away.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
away.blurb: The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. home.headline: Notre Dame football could get one of its best defensive players back from injury for SMU game
home.blurb: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - One of Notre Dame’s top players on defense might return to the field for the first time since Week 1 when the Fighting Irish host SMU this upcoming Saturday. According to the team’s latest availability report, safety Brauntae Johnson has been upgraded from out to questionable. Several other Notre Dame starters on both sides of the ball are either out or questionable for Saturday’s game. Linebacker Drayk Bowen has been ruled out for the third consecutive game after suffering a right ankle injury against Navy . Cornerback DJ McKinney will miss his fourth consecutive game because of a right ankle injury suffered in Notre Dame’s loss to BYU . Starting defensive linemen Francis Brewu and Jason Onye are listed as questionable for the third consecutive week. Neither has played since being injured against Navy. Starting left tackle Will Black is also questionable after suffering a concussion Saturday against Boston College . Offensive linemen Charles Jagusah and Chris Terek are no longer listed on the injury report and will return to practice this week. Freeman said their return will be similar to Johnson’s, with the team evaluating how they respond in practice. Johnson, a preseason AP second-team All-American , has been sidelined since injuring his left foot in the season opener against Wisconsin . Head coach Marcus Freeman said Monday that he will be integrated back into practice to see how his body responds and whether he has an opportunity to play against SMU. Full Notre Dame availability report Will Black, offensive lineman — concussion Francis Brewu, defensive lineman — left knee Brauntae Johnson, safety — left foot Jason Onye, defensive lineman — right knee Drayk Bowen, linebacker — right ankle Christopher Burgess Jr., defensive lineman — left tibia Tiki Hola, defensive lineman — right knee DJ McKinney, cornerback — right ankle Stay up to date on local news with WNDU on-air and online. home.headline: Notre Dame football regains two former starters for SMU week practice
home.blurb: The Fort Wayne product, out since the first half of the season opener against Wisconsin, will return to practice on Tuesday and go from there. Johnson had hoped to make it back in time for the Miami game on Nov. 7, but his foot wasn’t close enough to 100% for that to happen. If it’s determined that he needs more practice time before facing an opponent, Johnson will be held out against the Mustangs and pointed toward the regular-season finale at Syracuse “This is the next phase of his progression in terms of return to play,” Freeman said. Left tackle Will Black is questionable with a concussion suffered after 27 offensive snaps against Boston College. Styles Prescod took over for the final 47 snaps without apparent issue. Defensive tackles Francis Brewu and Jason Onye remain questionable with knee injuries suffered in the first quarter against Navy on Halloween, but there’s finally some good news for hard-luck offensive lineman Charles Jagusah. Sixteen months after suffering a broken left humerus in a utility vehicle accident, the senior guard/tackle has been upgraded to questionable. Jagusah has undergone at least five surgical procedures as he deals with nerve damage in his upper arm, including a bone graft on March 18. “This is the next phase for him,” Freeman said. “That doesn’t mean he’ll go out there and start on Saturday, but that means he is actually practicing starting this week. That is huge. That’s amazing for that young man that has been through so much to be at the point now he can return to practice.” “He’s been training and rehabbing,” Irish coach Marcus Freeman said Monday Nov. 16. “We’re going to try to integrate him back into practice and see how his body responds. There are some football-specific movements that you do in practice that you can’t simulate in rehab.” Freeman noted the Rock Island, IL product has appeared in postseason games for the Irish, including the 2024 College Football Playoff semifinal and title games, but he’s yet to play a home game in college. “He’s never stepped on the field in a game at Notre Dame Stadium,” Freeman said. “If he can help us and we can find a role, how cool would that be to do that on Saturday? His journey has been amazing in terms of the things he’s overcome.” Senior offensive lineman Chris Terek, coming off right knee surgery in August, has been removed from the injury report as well. Mike Berardino covers Notre Dame football for the South Bend Tribune and NDInsider.com. Follow him on social media @MikeBerardino.

picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Missouri game glance, opening odds, and early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 17, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Can the Cats get back on track? Nine days ago, Kentucky Football was in the College Football Playoff conversation. Now, the Wildcats are trying to save a season that was turning into something special. The 21-14 loss to Florida on Saturday night at Kroger Field hurt more than most. Kentucky came in as a three-point favorite at home against a 5-4 Gators team. The Cats took a 7-2 lead into halftime and still led 14-13 going into the fourth quarter. Then Florida took over. Aaron Philo ran for 102 yards, the Gators ran for 211 as a team, and Kentucky managed just 61 rushing yards on 27 carries. That’s a season low for a team that came in averaging almost 164 per game. Will Stein didn’t sugarcoat it afterward. He said his team came up short in all three phases. That one stings because of how good this season had been. This was the team that went to College Station and beat No. 9 Texas A&M by 10. It came back from 17 down to win in overtime at South Carolina, beat No. 10 LSU 35-34 in overtime and sent the fans onto the field, then won in Norman. Kentucky was 7-1 and ranked in the top ten of the CFP rankings. Back-to-back losses to Tennessee and Florida later, the playoff dream is just about gone. But there’s still a lot to play for. Kentucky is 7-3 and bowl eligible with two games left: at Missouri and Louisville at home. Win both, then win a bowl game, and Kentucky reaches 10 wins. The program has only done that four times in its history: 1950, 1977, 2018 and 2021. In Stein’s first year, against what his own players called a whole lot of doubt back in August, that would be a remarkable finish. It starts Saturday night in Columbia. Matchup: Kentucky (7-3) at Missouri (6-4, 3-4 SEC) When: Saturday, Nov. 21, 7:30 p.m. ET Where: Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium, Columbia, MO. TV: SEC Network Odds: Missouri -6.5, over/under 50.5 (FanDuel) All-time series: Kentucky leads 9-5 Last meeting: Missouri won 38-21 in Lexington in 2023 Opponent at a Glance: Missouri Tigers Head coach: Eli Drinkwitz (7th season) Missouri started the year ranked No. 25 in the preseason polls. For a while, it looked like the Tigers were exactly who people thought they were. They blew out Florida 45-17, held Texas A&M to six points in a 27-6 win and beat Arkansas by 24. The problem is what happened against good teams. Missouri lost at Mississippi State in September, lost 31-3 at Ole Miss, lost 34-20 at home to Texas and just got rolled 48-21 by No. 1 Georgia in Athens. Two straight losses ended the Tigers’ playoff hopes. The Georgia game was ugly from the first snap. Quarterback Austin Simmons threw an interception on the first play, Georgia scored two plays later, and Missouri was down 31 at halftime. Drinkwitz called it “not a good plan offensively or defensively,” and the Tigers went 2-for-11 on third down. Missouri 2026 Results W 54-14 vs. Arkansas-Pine Bluff W 38-21 vs. Kansas W 27-17 vs. Troy L 31-24 at Mississippi State W 45-17 vs. Florida W 27-6 vs. Texas A&M L 31-3 at Ole Miss W 34-10 at Arkansas L 34-20 vs. Texas L 48-21 at Georgia Players to Know QB Austin Simmons: He won the job over Matt Zollers in the spring and opened the season 17 of 19 for 252 yards and four touchdowns. When he gets protection he can pick you apart. RB Ahmad Hardy: A preseason AP First Team All-American and the engine of the run game. Kentucky’s run defense has to be better than it was against Florida. RB Jamal Roberts: The second back in a deep backfield. WR Donovan Olugbode: Simmons’ favorite target and the guy they go to on third down. OL Cayden Green: A preseason Second Team All-American who anchors the line. Keys to the Game Fix the run defense. Florida ran 48 times for 211 yards and wore Kentucky down in the second half. Missouri will try the exact same thing with Hardy. If Kentucky can’t set the edge, it’s going to be a long night. Get the run game going again. Kentucky’s offense works when the run sets up Kenny Minchey. Sixty-one rushing yards won’t win in the SEC, let alone on the road at night. Attack the secondary. Pass defense has been Missouri’s weak spot all year. Georgia’s Gunner Stockton went 18 of 24 for 252 yards. Minchey needs to take his shots. Start fast. Missouri has started slow on the road and on the ropes. Kentucky has led into the second half against Alabama, Tennessee, and Florida and lost all three. The second half is where this team has to grow up. Win the turnover battle. Kentucky’s big wins this year came down to a play here and there. Simmons has been careless with the ball against good defenses. Make him pay. Our Early Prediction This one comes down to which team handles adversity better. Both are coming off back-to-back losses, and both had playoff hopes that are now gone. Missouri has the home field and is favored by almost a touchdown. Kentucky has the head coach who has won close games all year. What gives me some hope is the bounce back. After Alabama blew them out, the Cats went on the road and beat Texas A&M. Stein has had a whole week to get this team’s attention after being called out for not looking like themselves. I think Kentucky responds. It won’t be pretty, but the Cats grind out a road win and stay alive for a 10-win season. Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. As for who could replace Bobo, Georgia does have options. The Bulldogs are likely to turn to either Cortez Smith or Malachi Toliver. Smith was working at center at the end of Georgia’s game last week. Toliver does have previous starting experience, filling in for three games last season when Bobo missed time because of hand and foot injuries. Georgia could also move Helton down to center. If that were to happen, perhaps Gaston moves to guard and Georgia could play either Ekene Ogboko or Jah Jackson at right tackle. Georgia does have one of the best offensive lines in the country, as the Bulldogs were one of 10 teams named as a semifinalist for the Joe Moore Award this week. Potentially not having Bobo will test this unit, especially with all the calls Bobo makes at the line of scrimmage. More will fall on the shoulders of quarterback Gunner Stockton as well. “It’s important for us to set the tone because, like, team run on Tuesdays, it’s the same way,” Glover said this week. “We’ve got to set the tone in order for us to have a good run game.” Georgia will face a stout Missouri front, as the Tigers ranked third in the SEC in run defense. home.headline: Major injury update for Georgia Football-Missouri game: Why It Really Matters for the Bulldogs
home.blurb: But the Bulldogs have been struck by injuries at critical positions the last two seasons in the CFP. In 2024, Georgia football starting QB Carson Beck suffered a season-ending injury in the SEC Championship Game - paving the way for Gunner Stockton to make his first career start against Norte Dame in the Sugar Bowl. That injury coupled with turnovers turned out to be too much for the Dawgs to overcome. Only two players are listed on Georgia football's injury report - DL Josh Horton and LB Amaris Williams. Williams was expected to be out, but Horton is a new addition to the injury repot. Horton is listed as questionable for the contest; Williams is listed as out, which means he will not play in the contest. Meanwhile, Missouri has four players listed as out: DL Langden Kitchen, RB Malae Fonoti, OL Josh Atkins and TE Gavin Hoffman. It should be noted that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss is listed as probable for the Rebels' game this weekend at Oklahoma. He joins a a list of 17 other Rebels on the injury report after Georgia's 42-7 beating of Ole Miss in Oxford. The Dawgs, on the whole, continue to be pretty healthy in the grand scheme of things. Should Isiah Canion and Chauncey Bowens return to full health the Bulldogs could become even lethal on the offensive side of the ball. Coach Kirby Smart said earlier this week that Bowens was not 100% healthy. Meanwhile, it will be curious to see if Amaris Williams will return this season. He suffered an ALC injury in the spring, and although the timeline would be tight, it is not out of the question that he could return to play in the playoffs the same way WR George Pickens did at the end of the 2021 season. Pickens also had an ACL injury around the same time that year. home.headline: Missouri football injury updates: Official SEC report Wednesday before Georgia
home.blurb: “We were very fortunate. When you watch it, it looks bad, but the cleat was not in the ground, which is a real relief there,” Mizzou head coach Eli Drinkwitz said Tuesday. “So, anticipate him trying to practice today, and we'll monitor that situation as it goes. … He was out in practice yesterday (Monday), and he is probably as tough a competitor as I've been around, so nothing would shock me more than if he wasn’t playing. But, again, I don’t know how his body will respond to that injury.” The Tigers did, as expected, rule out defensive end Langden Kitchen, who Drinkwitz said Tuesday had surgery on his knee after sustaining an injury during the Tigers’ loss to Texas this past Saturday. Kitchen will not play for Mizzou again this season. As it has since SEC play started, Mizzou ruled out running back Malae Fonoti, who is out for the season, right tackle Josh Atkins, who Eli Drinkwitz said he does not expect to be available this year, and tight end Gavin Hoffman. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable; doubtful; out. The reports are not technically injury reports, which some teams — Mizzou often included — provided in years prior. Instead, they are lists that include any players ruled unavailable or possibly unavailable for upcoming games. That could be for any number of reasons, including but not limited to injuries. Per MU head coach Eli Drinkwitz, Lee was expected to practice for the Tigers on Tuesday.
