away.headline: Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Stanford: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies?
away.source: Virginia Tech Hokies On SI on MSN
away.blurb: The player availability report, which was first used for the 2025 season, provides five types of designations prior to game day: available, probable, questionable, doubtful, and out. A player being available means that they are not designated on the list. Here's how the availability report shakes out by position: This article was originally published on www.si.com/college/virginiatech as Initial Availability Report Released for Virginia Tech-Stanford: Who's In, Out, TBD For Hokies? . BLACKSBURG — After a 23-point loss to SMU in Dallas, Virginia Tech football takes on Stanford in a Saturday night showdown in Lane Stadium. Ahead of the clash, the ACC revealed the initial player availability report for both teams this week. Here's the list of players posted on the initial availability report, organized by status: Offensive Line: 4 (Wright, Austin, Bright, Terry) Wide Receiver: 2 (Peterkin, Stuewe) Virginia Tech (6-3, 3-3 ACC) opened its season with four straight wins for the first time since 2017, defeating VMI (73-3), Old Dominion (44-21), Maryland (35-26) and Boston College (21-14). The Hokies claimed their largest margin of victory since 1922 with their 70-point win over the Keydets Sept. 5, and they avenged their loss from Sept. 13, 2025, against the Monarchs which forced the ouster of then-head coach — and Virginia Tech's current defensive coordinator/linebackers coach — Brent Pry one day later. Against Maryland, the Hokies broke a 15-game Power Four non-conference losing streak dating back to 2017, beating the Terrapins by nine. Sept. 26's victory in Boston College was harder to come by, but amid a nor'easter, sophomore running back Jeffrey Overton Jr.'s career-high 209 rushing yards proved enough for the Hokies to escape with the victory. The Hokies sustained their first loss on Oct. 2, falling to Pitt 35-33 after conceding a 35-10 run over two-plus quarters. Virginia Tech made a nine-point rally to pull within two, but fifth-year kicker John Love's 36-yard field goal attempt for the win was ruled no good. The Hokies lost to Cal 25-20 in Berkeley the following week, ceding the game-winning touchdown to the Golden Bears with 18 seconds remaining. Virginia Tech returned to the win column on Oct. 17, defeating Georgia Tech 34-24 in a contest where it led 24-3 at intermission. The Hokies then became bowl eligible with a 20-16 win over Clemson — their first over the Tigers since 2007 in their trip to Memorial Stadium since 2012. Virginia Tech, however, fell in a 51-28 blowout at SMU Nov. 6, allowing season-highs in both points (51) and total yards of offense (569). The 51 points the Mustangs totaled on Virginia Tech were the most allowed by a Hokies team since the 2021 Pinstripe Bowl against Maryland, while the 569 yards Tech allowed were the most since Oct. 10, 2020, against North Carolina. away.headline: Virginia Tech injury report for Stanford paints a promising outlook for Justin Terry
away.blurb: In the Hokies Week 3 35-26 victory over Maryland, Virginia Tech lost offensive lineman Justin Terry in the first half, and he has been out since then. However, there could be some light at the end of the tunnel for Terry in terms of getting back onto the field, and it might come as soon as this upcoming weekend when Stanford visits . That certainly would be a positive, but a return on Saturday night feels a little ahead of schedule. It would be surprising if he were rushed back from an injury to play against the Cardinal. Franklin said that Terry will likely be a game-time decision. "It's not like we're totally through it," Franklin said. "We still got the rest of the week, and probably will come down to either a game-time decision, or it will be he's cleared, but we still don't feel like he's gotten enough reps." Three regular-season games remain in the 2026 campaign, and already at 6-3, the Hokies are guaranteed a bowl game later next month before the attention shifts toward the 2027 season. Getting Terry back would be a big addition, but even if he does return this weekend, his snaps might be limited; just his presence would be big for Grunkemeyer and the rest of the offense. Virginia Tech football comes out of bye week getting healthier in one pivotal area Going all the way back to the summer, injuries along the offensive line have been an issue for first-year Virginia Tech football coach James Franklin. Then, it carried over into the regular season, where it seems that when it rains, it pours. James Franklin gives positive Justin Terry injury update ahead of Stanford game According to Andy Bitter of Tech Sideline , Terry was going through 1-on-1 drills with the D-linemen. After practice, Franklin gave an update on his linemen ahead of Stanford visiting on Saturday night at Lane Stadium. "So today was really the first day that we've been able to have him for everything," Franklin said , per Virginia Tech Athletics ' YouTube . "We've been kind of working him in slowly. Drills, (individuals), one-on-ones. So today was the first day we've kind of had him for everything. So he's getting closer, and it's positive for us.'' Virginia Tech's offensive line can use all the help it can get If and when Terry comes back, it'll be a welcome sight for Hokies fans. To say that the offensive line has struggled this season would be an understatement. Some of that is because of injuries, while some of it is because there have been guys moved around to different positions. Consistency is key and it feels like there hasn't been much of it this season. Virginia Tech has struggled to protect quarterback Ethan Grunkemeyer at times, despite the Penn State transfer having a good year statistically. Then there is the running game that the Hokies have desperately tried to get going. away.blurb: While Craig will be available on Saturday, it appears he still not be 100% and that means the Horned Frogs could rely on sophomore quarterback Adam Schobel. Schobel played about half a dozen snaps against the Wildcats, rushing for three yards on three carries. “I love Adam; we came in at the same time. He was a freshman when I transferred in,” Pimpton said. “So I have a great relationship with Adam. I’m pretty sure Jay’s going to tough it and play.
